children: Gold edges higher in early Asian trade, recovering some ground after shedding 4.5% last week but lingering at around one-year lows. The precious metal has struggled as renewed bets of rate hikes by the Fed fuel dollar strength. Elevated bond yields are also dimming the appeal of non-interest-bearing gold. Political pressure for more defense spending and the reversal of healthcare cuts could widen U.S. fiscal deficits, reinforcing the longer-term argument for holding gold, says Chris Weston at Pepperstone. But gold's recent moves suggest that a compelling long-term fiscal narrative doesn't necessarily protect an asset when the dollar is rising and real yields are sharply higher, he says. Gold is 0.2% higher at $3,891/ounce. (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)
